Victoria vase

Marco Zanini’s porcelain vase for Memphis: a ribbed lilac column with a blue-and-yellow fan on top.

Source
Art Institute of Chicago: Victoria Vase (1986.411a)
Creator
Marco Zanini; made by Memphis S.R.L.
Made
1982
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods

Evidence

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Art Institute lists the vase as designed by Marco Zanini and made by Memphis S.R.L., Milan, 1982; porcelain with enamel decoration, 64.8 cm high. It was purchased from Memphis s.r.l. AIC record.

The record gives separate dimensions for a flat top piece, 43.5 × 35.9 × 1.4 cm. AIC record.

Observed

  • The lower body is a lilac column of stacked discs and ridged, bead-like swellings on a round foot.
  • A flat quarter-circle sits upright on top, split on the diagonal into deep blue and yellow.
  • The yellow half has a scalloped outer edge; the blue half has a smooth curve.
  • All surfaces are glossy and flat in color, without pattern.

Why it belongs

The vase stacks unrelated forms, a turned column and a flat cut-out, and gives them unrelated colors. This joining of parts that do not match is typical of Memphis objects.

Borrow

Top a solid, repetitive base with one flat, cut-out shape in contrasting colors.

Use a scalloped or wavy edge against a straight or smooth one.
